positions.title: iOS Engineer
positions.description:
At Le Tote, I maintain/expand the core app and build/maintain other iOS apps and libraries as necessary. I play a highly collaborative role with product, design, and other engineering teams as features are being designed and built.

Major Accomplishments:

* Recommended Products - Here, the user likes or dislikes each product in a set of 40 new products once a week. Because liked products tend to lead to better liked totes, this feature increased tote satisfaction and tote ratings. It has also contributed to higher engagement because users enjoy liking and disliking the products.

* Tote Swap Experience Redesign - Le Tote lets you see and swap out items before having the tote shipped. We redesigned the swapping process in late 2016 to early 2017. After the iOS implementation was added, a greater proportion of swaps were performed on iOS in comparison to other platforms. In addition, a greater proportion of tote confirmations occurred on iOS.

* GraphQL Support - The Letote Engineering organization decided in 2016 to switch to GraphQL for future API services. This led to a number of challenges, and the iOS team decided to build a query formatter library to decrease development time. I built the original codebase, and I've maintained it as other iOS developers have requested features. We continue to build new features here and make adjustments as developers make new requests.

* Referrals - This feature allows customers to receive credit for sharing the app with their friends. I have worked with product and design to ensure that we take full advantage of system contacts, messaging and social media sharing capabilities. This has led to and increase in referral customers.

Tech:

My GraphQL library - https://github.com/LeToteTeam/Stardaze. An app that is primarily Swift with some Objective-C in libraries. A few small helper apps also in Swift.

positions.title: iOS Developer
positions.description:
At Keeptruckin, I maintained the main iOS app and built new features.  Keeptruckin is an app that allows truckers to spend less time filling out their logs while allowing trucking companies to maintain more accurate logs for their truckers by eliminating the manual effort of filling out forms. The app maintained compliance with United States federal and state laws. The app also read from a device connected to the truck engine that collected odometer, speed, and other information, showing it in a readable UI and passing it on to the server as necessary.

Technical Challenges:

* Data Consistency - The iOS app received events for every start and stop event from the truck's engine connected device. In addition, we would send and receive information from our web server on a regular basis. Having a firm understanding of grand central dispatch was essential to this job. Much of the work involved receiving large amounts of data from the truck and processing it while maintaining a good user experience that reflected the most up to date reflection of the data. If there were ever conflicts between the information received from the truck and the information received from the web server, we would also need to handle that in a consistent expected way.

* Specifications - Because truckers drive through many different legal zones through the course of a single day, keeping very clear product specifications dealing with different legal zones and different timezones was very important.

Tech:
GCD, FMDB, SQL, Bluetooth

Had a blast shaping and being shaped by the culture of a very early stage startup.

projects.title: Rap Genius Clone
projects.description:
One of my first projects with Ruby on Rails was a clone of RapGenius. I don't maintain this any longer, and when I look back at the code, I shudder a little bit. That said, I learned a lot in the process. Here are some takeaways that I gained working on this project.

Processing Text in HTML is Difficult
There are selectors for tags, but getting part of the text of a p, or getting text that spans over multiple divs is much more difficult.  Another thing that people don't often think about is that when you write html tags in a standard way, with a tag opener or closer on one line, and the content in between, return lines are introduced into the file. These return lines do not affect the browser's parsing of the file, but when processing text from multiple divs, they must be taken into account.

Choose the Right Tool or Build a More Appropriate Tool
I used several features built into Twitter Bootstrap that needed to be highly customized. The customization process was more than likely more difficult than building the same thing with Javascript and CSS would have been. Using the customized tools was also buggy and inconsistent. Since then, I have spent much longer considering the tools to use for a particular task, and I have found that in many cases, the best tool is pure Javascript and CSS.
